challenge.better_approach: Freezing the relay's clock would reach into sudo_relay from a system_word proof (RULE 1). Stripping the stamp at the compare is local and enough.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That the stamp is the only per-call difference; measured: two --status calls differ in the timestamp alone.
challenge.prior_art: Grepped system_word proofs for a timestamp strip: none. The relay's line shape is [sudo_relay] <ISO>  <words>.

answers.falsifier: Done when the relay tooth compares through _untimed and passes, and _untimed equates lines that differ only in timestamp. Wrong intent if the fold should change the relay's output beyond the clock.
answers.from_idea: none, because the orchestrator ordered it from its Linux reseal of 2026-11-13; the red proof is cairn/tools/system_word/proofs/test_system_word.py
answers.how: test_system_word.py gains _untimed(text), a regex replacing every ISO timestamp, and test_sudo_relay_takes_uppercase_status_flag compares stdout and stderr through it. A new declaring proof checks _untimed equates clock-only differences and keeps word differences, and that the relay tooth compares through it and passes.
answers.traces_to: Law 3 (a proof that flips on the clock measures the clock, not the fold); Law 8 (a hollow-free green must be repeatable).
answers.what: system_word's relay tooth compares `cairn sudorelay --status` against `--STATUS` with every ISO timestamp taken out, so the tooth stops being a coin toss on the second turning over.

bullets.text: The relay tooth compared two timestamped outputs byte for byte; red whenever the second turned over. It now compares with the clock out.
